Applicant present: Leslie Herman, Director of Parks and Recreation.

Ms. Herman stated that she appreciated the board's collaboration with the modifications to the Meadow Lane Park restrooms during the February 15, 2024, Board of Architectural Review meeting. After said meeting, Ms. Herman reached out to staff and decided that they would like to go with a darker color roof for the bathrooms. Mr. Layer asked Ms. Herman if she knew when the project would move forward, to which she replied she was hoping the installation would happen after fall. With no further questions or comments from the board or the public, a motion was in order.

Item No 7: Request for approval of a sign for Pure Green, located at 136 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1262475-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center Zoning District; filed by Chelsey Bashorun, Signarama.

Applicant Present: Anthony Bashorun

Mr. Bashorun stated that he is proposing a façade sign with the business standard branding illuminated on the raceway to match the color of the façade. Ms. van Doorn asked if samples were provided for the green color. Unfortunately, the applicant did not have samples but noted that PMS color information was included in the staff report. 

Mr. Layer stated that the center was redesigned entirely for the signs to be white with accents that would follow each other. He recommended that the Pure Green sign follow the same pattern. Having the signs coordinated and harmonious with the other signs is important in strip centers. 

Ms. van Doorn stated she was not opposed to the green and suggested maybe incorporating some white into the design to be consistent. The board discussed how the original theme for the center was developed and different possibilities for incorporating white into the Pure Green sign. One suggestion was to use a perforated sign. During the daylight, the sign could be as proposed, and at night it would be white with perforated green for the logo.  The applicant liked the suggestion as well as the rest of the board members. 

Public comment: Ms. Carol Wolfand stated she understood the importance of continuity and signage as it holds the community’s eye and makes complexes look updated and fluid.  However, she doesn’t agree with changing the national chain logo to keep that effect. National Logos spends a lot of money on its product sales and the taxes they pay to the town because people recognize their logo and shop there which is important to the business in the community. Before taking a business, logo and trying to align it for color it should be considered how it affects the business owners who are the ones who spent money to be in the town to do business. Ms. Wolfand added that she liked the suggestions made by the board.

 Ms. van Doorn stated that she also has sympathy for someone’s branding and agrees with the argument that the board should work hard to have consistency while also keeping in mind the importance of brand recognition and the color scheme that is part of it.  Ms. Hanley agreed and noted that is the reason she provided a suggestion that allowed keeping the logo. The lighting, however, is different because a brand could not be consistent or good for the neighborhood when lit. 

 Mr. Layer stated that the charter does not state the board has restrictions in terms of the brand, it states that they’re to look at the community overall. Is it good for the community, is it keeping with the harmony of its neighbors, is it aesthetically pleasing, does it have integrity? The boards have historically tried to work with the people to see if there’s a compromise in terms of the way it fits with the center and still achieving their logo. The discussion continued. 

Mr. Layer made a motion to defer the request for a sign for Pure Green, located at 136 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1262475-BAR, in the AC, Avenue Center Zoning District to allow the applicant to incorporate some of the suggestions into another design and allow the applicant to provide the board with samples.

Motion: Mr. Layer 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 136 Maple Ave W - Pure Green - Sign

Item No 8: Request for approval of exterior modifications at 317 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1264264-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district; filed by Robert Froh, Robinson Sidewalk Project, Town of Vienna, Project Contact.

Applicant Present: Robert Froh, Department of Public Works

Mr. Froh stated that they’re building a sidewalk along Pleasant St. To build the sidewalk they need to build a retaining wall due to an existing embankment in front of the building occupied by Verizon. The applicant is proposing the construction of a reinforced concrete 4-foot retaining wall with a brick face at the back of the public sidewalk with an ornamental handrail mounted on top of the railing, that will be powder coated and painted in black. The retaining wall will be in the public right of way except for where it ties back into the embankment on the two sides. 

Ms. van Doorn asked if the railing would be mounted into the cap piece or the ground. Mr. Froh replied that it would be mounted into the cap piece with a reinforced concrete wall underneath it. They will drill through the cap and drill into the reinforcer into the concrete wall and mount it that way. He also noted that the existing stairs encroach into the right of way by 1.2 feet. The applicant is proposing to leave the existing stairs in place, the wall will be at the back of the right-of-way line which will put the sidewalk 1 foot in front and move the stairs an extra 2 ½ inches so it flush with the last riser so that it won’t be tripping hazard. As the discussion continued and the renderings were reviewed the board had some questions/concerns about the landscaping, the configuration of the driveway, and the sidewalk. It was noted that the board was only reviewing the request for the retaining wall, however, the board provided the applicant with a few recommendations to try to re-establish as much green within the context of the design. 

The board reviewed the brick sample provided to them. There was some confusion with the sample and the picture displayed on the screen. Ms. Hanley pointed out that they were not the same. After discussion, the applicant realized that he left the paver sample in his office. While the sample was being retrieved from the office by staff the board continued to review the application. Recommendations were made to possibly replace the tree that would be removed due to grading issues that wouldn’t allow saving the tree and doing the grading necessary to create the streetscape. Additionally, some suggestions were made for the step reconfiguration to avoid possible complications in the future. However, the applicant would rather let the property owner take care of that in the future if they redevelop. The discussion continued and the board provided additional suggestions/recommendations for the configuration of the sidewalk and driveway. 

Mr. Layer made a motion to approve the request for exterior modifications at 317 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1264264-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district as follows:

• The retaining wall, the brick, the railing, and the material for the sidewalk configuration were approved as presented. 
• The item was approved with the stipulation to increase green or landscaping on the upper side of the wall where there is more space.
• Adding the possibility of installing a tree for the removal of the one that was on the application that is on the private property.        

The board recommended considering some methodologies to raise the paving to a certain degree to mitigate some of the severity of the slope coming off the site and consider slightly shifting it if there can be a better grading afforded with the redesign. 

Motion: Mr. Layer 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe 
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 317 Maple Ave W - Town of Vienna - Exterior Modification

Item No 9: Request for approval of exterior modifications at 210 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1264611-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district; filed by Robert Froh, Robinson Sidewalk Project, Town of Vienna, Project Contact.

Applicant Present: Robert Froh, Department of Public Works

Mr. Froh stated he is proposing to move the curb 4 feet into the right of way to gain additional room to build a sidewalk with a retaining wall. The wall is proposed to have a cap and a brick face. The applicant is also proposing bollards mounted on top of the retaining wall. The bollards are not to stop a vehicle but rather to create a visual break between the public sidewalk, the retaining wall, and the jiffy lube property. The retaining wall is approximately 30 feet long. The applicant is removing the existing landscaping to make space for the sidewalk but will provide landscaping to compensate for the loss of the shrubs. The board reviewed the application and stated the following:

Mr. Layer voiced his concern about the possibility of people not realizing they’re going to step off a wall because of the way the applicant is proposing the wall cap. Mr. Froh stated there is a concrete area next to the building and a curb that rises 6 inches to which they will have the wall at the same height on top of the curb. The discussion continued and Mr. Layer suggested using a rail vs. bollards. In his opinion, the bollards would not survive. Mr. Froh responded that the downfall of using a rail is that if it gets hit it will be more difficult to replace because you will have to replace the whole length of the rail vs when using a bollard if you hit one bollard it won’t be as much damage to the wall and it would be easier o replace. The discussion continued and Mr. Layer asked the applicant if he considered using steel bollards with sleeves that go over vs standard bollards, this way if the bollard gets hit they can replace the sleeve. Another suggestion was putting joints at the part that would receive the impact load (one joint on each side of the wall) so that if something strikes that particular part it will just crack that section of the wall. Mr. Froh responded that is something that they incorporate into the design. 

Ms Hanley commented on the brick color. The light color makes the dirt visible. She wondered if the applicant considered a contrasting color as opposed to matching the building. Mr. Froh stated that he presented the owner with two color options and decided on the color matching the building. After agreeing with Ms. Hanley’s concern the applicant noted that he will be fine with changing the color to match the Maple Ave pavers which are the same pavers the used on the Verizon property. 

Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to approve the exterior modifications at 210 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1264611-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district as follows:

• Separation of the retaining wall at the bollards.
• Change the brick as stated during the discussion.

Motion: Mr. O’Keefe
Second: Mr. Layer 
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 210 Maple Ave W - Town of Vienna - Exterior Modification

Item No 13: Request for approval of exterior modifications to the Iris Building, located at 305 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1262431-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district; filed by Adam Ehrlich, Alpha Consulting Enterprises, LLC, Project Contact.

Applicants Present: Nay Sabusi and Adam Ehrlich

Ms. Sabusi stated that the request for the exterior modifications is to paint the standing seam roof, standing seam canopy, and window trim of the building with Sherwin Williams Navy Blue 6244. Color Sherwin Williams Loyal Blue 6510 was also provided as an alternative color. The applicant chose the blue colors to represent her tenants who are mostly in the medical field. 

Ms. Hanley asked for clarification on the window trim. The applicant said they would like to paint the window trim to match the blue to keep it consistent. The board reviewed the application and suggested the following:

• The alternate color (Loyal Blue 6510) was preferred since it matched better with the shopping center across the street, and it was a lighter color. 
• Recommendation for the window panels – first prime, then paint with an acrylic latex semi-gloss paint. 
• Recommendation for the roof- add tint to the primer to make it dark enough so that the finish coat latex will cover one coat. 
• Suggestion- consider using brake metal for the window frames. 

Ms. van Doorn made a motion to approve the request for exterior modifications to the Iris Building, located at 305 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1262431-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West zoning district as submitted with the provision that the roof color be Loyal Blue with direct-to-metal paint for the roof and canopy and the window trim be painted in a semi-gloss exterior acrylic in Sherwin Williams Loyal Bue 6510.

Motion: Ms. van Doorn
Second: Mr. Layer
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 305 Maple Ave W - Iris Building - Exterior Modifications

Item No 14: Request for approval of a master sign plan for the Iris Building, located at 305 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1263989-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Zoning District; filed by Adam Ehrlich, Alpha Consulting Enterprises, LLC., Project Contact.

Applicants Present: Nay Sabusi and Adam Ehrlich

Ms. Sabusi is proposing a master sign plan for the current and future tenant spaces for the building façade and the pylon sign.  The primary tenants who are in the medical field will be on the 1st floor. The applicant is proposing channel signs for the first-floor and cabinet box signs for the second-floor tenants which will make it easier when swapping out tenants. The applicant provided an alternative selection of White acrylic faces and Black letters for the cabinet box signs. The board reviewed the application and stated the following:
• Box signs – maybe use a blue background with white lettering.
• Box sign- The kelvin level should be within the 3500 range. 
• Discussion on the color palette for the channel signs to ensure there is a boundary in staying consistent with the color palette. 
• Concern with tenant Health Check Urgent Care having four colors. 
• Suggestion– perforated channel letters for the wordings “Health Check” so that at night it would be white, and the wordings “Urgent Care” be red. As it pertains to the master sign plan this would allow the tenants to have one color coming through illuminated at night and the other colors can be utilized in the daytime. 
• Suggestion- tenant sign black perforated during the day and illuminated at night. 

After the discussion, the applicant stated she preferred the alternate cabinet box sign because the option is bolder. It will give the tenants a little more after not being able to use their designs.  The board agreed with the applicant's decision. 

The board reviewed the proposed pylon sign and voiced their concerns about the entire pylon sign being painted blue. The board recommended maintaining the shingles brown or possibly painting the sign blue and maintaining the original shingles. After further discussion, a motion was in order. 

Mr. Layer made a motion to approve the request for a master sign plan for the Iris Building, located at 305 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1263989-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Zoning District as follows:

The Box Signs:
• The alternate sign choice with Loyal Blue trim and Loyal Blue lettering.

The current Tenant Channel Letter Sign :
• Logo in the proposed color scheme.
• Wordings “Health” & “Check” in the proposed colors but perforated so that at night the words show as white.
• Urgent Care to remain as presented.

Future Tenant Channel Letter Sign :
• The logo should be in the master sign plan approved colors. 
• Channel letters should be in the master sign plan with approved colors and perforated so that at night the words of the sign show as white. 

The Pylon Sign roof is to remain its current color and the sign board as submitted.

Motion: Mr. Layer 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried

The board realized that the Kelvin level was not included in the motion, so the item was reopened. Mr. O’Keefe made a motion to re-open item number 14 Request for approval of a master sign plan for the Iris Building, located at 305 Maple Ave W, Docket No. PF-1263989-BAR, in the AW, Avenue West Zoning District to which Mr. Layer seconded the motion. 

Ms. van Doorn made a motion to amend the initial motion to include that the Kelvin level for the signs does not exceed 3500 Kelvin. 

Motion: Ms. van Doorn 
Second: Mr. O’Keefe
Vote: 5-0
Motion Carried
EventItemTitle: 305 Maple Ave W - Iris Building - Master Sign Plan
